exposure: second-stage repeat cesarean delivery without an operative vaginal delivery attempt
Attempted operative vaginal delivery (with either forceps or vacuum) after trial of labor after cesarean delivery
trial of labor after cesarean delivery
Trial of labor after cesarean delivery with and without attempted operative vaginal delivery
fetal descent greater than +2 station at complete dilation
cohort: 1230 women who underwent a trial of labor after cesarean delivery who were at least 36 weeks gestation, had a live, singleton, nonanomalous gestation in cephalic presentation and reached second-stage labor with a fetal station of at least +2
finding: Attempted operative vaginal delivery in the setting of a trial of labor after cesarean delivery in the second stage with a fetal station of at least +2, resulted in a vaginal birth after cesarean delivery in most women and was not associated with increased adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes but was associated with a reduced frequency of endometritis compared with repeat cesarean delivery without operative vaginal delivery attempt.
mod_finding: Attempted operative vaginal delivery, in the context of trial of labor after cesarean, was associated with a reduced frequency of endometritis compared to repeat cesarean delivery without operative vaginal delivery attempt.
